wy_1_lower_bench_bozo_s_revenge.descent_text: A V-thread at the top is the descent anchor; it holds up well and can be backed up with a second screw or thread before rappelling off.
wy_1_lower_bench_bozo_s_revenge.approach: From the valley road, turn onto Hunter Creek Road and follow it to a two-track on the left that leads to a small parking area. A trail starting left of the lot climbs to the Lower Bench, where the north-facing flows sit high on the hillside above the valley. Bozo's Revenge is toward the right-hand end of the bench, past Joy After Pain.

wy_1_lower_bench_joy_after_pain.approach: From the valley road, turn onto Hunter Creek Road and follow it to a two-track on the left that leads to a small parking area. A trail starting left of the lot climbs to the Lower Bench, where the north-facing flows sit high on the hillside above the valley. Joy After Pain sits on the right side of the bench, with Pillars of the Community to its left and Bozo's Revenge to its right. The line follows a drainage with a steep curtain and pillar at the start and a final steep step high in the drainage.

wy_1_lower_bench_legal_at_last.descent_text: Climb the route and make a V-thread to rappel back down to the drainage. The base can be mixed if the ice has melted out, so carry sling material for threads.
wy_1_lower_bench_legal_at_last.approach: From the valley road, turn onto Hunter Creek Road and follow it to a two-track on the left that leads to a small parking area. A trail starting left of the lot climbs to the Lower Bench, where the north-facing flows sit high on the hillside above the valley. Legal At Last lies in the amphitheater above The Moratorium: climb or hike The Moratorium and keep going up the drainage until the route comes into view on the left side of the amphitheater.

wy_1_lower_bench_mean_streak.approach: From the valley road, turn onto Hunter Creek Road and follow it to a two-track on the left that leads to a small parking area. A trail starting left of the lot climbs to the Lower Bench, where the north-facing flows sit high on the hillside above the valley. Mean Streak is the central flow of the bench when it forms, between The One Hitter and The Moratorium, just left of Natural Immunity.

wy_1_lower_bench_pillars_of_the_communit.approach: From the valley road, turn onto Hunter Creek Road and follow it to a two-track on the left that leads to a small parking area. A trail starting left of the lot climbs to the Lower Bench, where the north-facing flows sit high on the hillside above the valley. Pillars of the Community is left of Joy After Pain along the bench; the first pitch is a narrow slot guarded by a chockstone.

wy_1_lower_bench_the_moratorium.descent_text: Rappel the route. Build a V-thread at the top of the second pitch if none is in place, and aim for the small shelf on the left at the top of the first pitch for the lower rappel. Leaving the screws from the first belay in place gives you something to clip while setting up. The last rappel is straightforward.
wy_1_lower_bench_the_moratorium.approach: Hunter Creek Road has a pull-off from which the route is visible, and a parking area on a two-track nearby also serves the bench. The approach crosses flat ground and then gains a lot of height to reach the base, and is widely regarded as the hardest part of the day. Snow can slow the climb up.

wy_1_lower_bench_the_one_hitter.approach: From the valley road, turn onto Hunter Creek Road and follow it to a two-track on the left that leads to a small parking area. A trail starting left of the lot climbs to the Lower Bench, where the north-facing flows sit high on the hillside above the valley. The One Hitter is at the left end of the bench, well left of The Moratorium.

wy_1_lower_valley_welcome_wagon.approach: Driving into the South Fork valley, Welcome Wagon is the first obvious flow up to the right, forming on volcanic cliffs just above the road. Park off the road and walk the short way up to the base.

wy_2_schoolhouse_creek_illogicicle_class.descent_text: Rappel the route from trees; bring webbing for slinging them. The same trees and V-thread anchors used on The Schoolhouse Route serve the lower part of the descent.
wy_2_schoolhouse_creek_illogicicle_class.approach: Park at the Ishawooa Mesa trailhead just before the South Fork Road splits toward Hunter Creek Road. Cross the sage prairie toward the drainage just left of the prominent Schoolhouse Spire and follow the drainage to the first pitches of The Schoolhouse Route. Classroom Bully carries on from the top of that route's third pitch, taking the left branch of the drainage.

wy_2_schoolhouse_creek_illogicicle_hangi.approach: Park at the Ishawooa Mesa trailhead just before the South Fork Road splits toward Hunter Creek Road, and take the Illogicicle drainage, the second drainage east of Schoolhouse Creek. The route is in the main amphitheater just right of the first pitch of Illogicicle; it is often climbed as a way around that pitch when it has not formed.

wy_2_schoolhouse_creek_illogicicle_illog.approach: Park at the Ishawooa Mesa trailhead just before the South Fork Road splits toward Hunter Creek Road. Cross the sagebrush, bear left around a small hill, and go up the main drainage toward its left fork, scrambling in places; the Illogicicle amphitheater is the second drainage east of Schoolhouse Creek. Snow slows the approach.

wy_2_schoolhouse_creek_illogicicle_the_s.descent_text: Rappel the route. The first pitch comes down from a V-thread and the pitches above use trees; bring webbing to sling them.
wy_2_schoolhouse_creek_illogicicle_the_s.approach: Park at the Ishawooa Mesa trailhead just before the South Fork Road splits toward Hunter Creek Road. Using the three-spired Schoolhouse Spire as a landmark, hike across the sage prairie to the drainage just left of it, then follow the drainage up to a fork and take the right-hand branch. The drainage is steep in places and needs care around chockstones and boulders.

wy_2_upper_bench_animal_rights_activist.approach: Start at the Boulder Basin trailhead on Hunter Creek Road and follow the Boulder Basin trail to its first switchback, where it turns back on itself nearly 180 degrees. From there, head up and left and follow the drainage to the base of the curtain.
